newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton rates unchanged in select buying.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton rates unchanged in select buying.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates remained unchanged on Tuesday amid select buying by mill owners and are likely to remain pegged at these levels for the next few days, dealers said.

"Only low-quality cotton is now left from the 1996/97 (July-June) crop," dealer Shamimul Haq said. "The prices will take a dip once the arrival of new crop picks up. But for the time being, the rates are likely to hover around these levels."
Exporters were sidelined after the government raised sales tax to 12.5 percent from 10 percent in the national budget for fiscal 1997/98 (July/June), he said.
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was traded between 2,000 ($49.39) and 2,200 rupees per maund (37.32 k.g), dealers said.
